nodes.title: About Ripple Lora Prompting
widgets_values:
The default prompt used by the workflow is:

_Use the reference video for motion, timing, camera movement, composition, and unchanged scene content, while consistently propagating the visual edit established in the first frame throughout the video._

For difficult edits, add a short description of the changed first frame. For example, describe the new lighting, object, material, style, or background that should remain consistent across the video.


--- -

**LORA Strength**

Recommended strength setting: 1.35
Increase the LoRA strength when the edit is not being carried through strongly enough. Decrease it when the output changes content that should remain unchanged

nodes.title: About Ripple Lora
widgets_values:
For more in-depth guide, read on the download page for the lora. 

**How it works:**
1. Input your video.
2. Edit and replace its first frame.

Use an image editor or LLM to change the first frame to how you want the video to look like. The input image matching closely the input video first frame (pose, composition etc) will give best results

**Useful applications include:**

- Adding Special Effects
- 3D model re/texturing
- Style Change
- Light source / time of day change
- Character Attribute Change
- Background Change
- Weather Change
- Archviz Retexturing
- Title/Logo Replacement
- Object Addition / Removal / Replacement
- Sharpening / Blurring

nodes.title: Video settings
widgets_values:
If low on Ram/Vram, try  768x512, 832x480 or 960x544.  With higher Vram you can try 1280x736 or 1920x1088

Width & height settings must be divisible by 32 + 1. 
Frame count must be divisible by 8 + 1. 

Running with invalid parameters **will not cause errors**. Instead, the flow will silently choose the closest valid parameters. 

**Length in seconds:**  try 5, 10 or 20. 

**FPS:** 24 or 25 (or 48 if your pc can run it)

nodes.title: Prompting LTX-2
widgets_values:
## LTX-2 Prompting Tips
1. **Core Actions**: Describe events and actions as they occur over time  
2. **Audio**: Describe sounds and dialogue needed for the scene  
3. **Reference Image**: Do not repeat details already present  
4. **Consistency**: Avoid instructions that do not match the reference image, as this will degrade results

nodes.title: Single pass vs 2 pass
widgets_values:
This workflow works best in single pass.
But feel free to try 2-pass. It might run faster, and better on lower spec computer (2nd pass does introduce some change at 2nd sampler though)

nodes.title: PREVENT IDENTITY MIXING + DARKENING
READ THIS — FORMAT + FOUR-PERSON SETUP
widgets_values:
## ONE WORKFLOW — SELECT THE FORMAT

Use **ASPECT — OFF: 9:16 | ON: 16:9** at the top of the graph.

- **OFF / false:** vertical 9:16, delivered at 1080×1920.
- **ON / true:** landscape 16:9, delivered at 1920×1080.

The switch controls the working width, working height, and final crop together. All other rules remain unchanged: use only the untouched source chunk, provide one backend-composited edited first frame for up to four mapped people, process eight-second chunks, and remux the untouched original audio after joining.

## BACKEND INPUT CONTRACT — 1 TO 4 PEOPLE

1. `source_video`: always use the untouched original. Never use a generated output as the next input.
2. `reference_images[1..4]`: one clear identity image per person.
3. `person_map`: keep a stable mapping, for example Reference 1 → tracked Person 1, across every chunk.
4. Before queueing this graph, detect/track the people and composite all requested replacements into the first source frame of **each** 8-second chunk.
5. Put that single composited frame into **EDITED FIRST FRAME — COMPOSITED 1–4 PEOPLE**. Do not append the loose portraits as guide frames.
6. Render chunks independently on the GPU workers, trim each result to its exact source-frame count, join in original order, and remux the untouched source audio.

The workflow performs the LTX/Ripple propagation. Person detection, tracking, identity-to-person mapping, and construction of the edited first frame belong in the backend preprocessing stage.

## POST-RENDER MASKED FACE LOCK

The selected 1080p frame batch now passes through the grouped masked face-lock branch before encoding. Leave node **1563** ON to use it. The backend must set both face-index strings in node **1564** to `0`, `0,1`, `0,1,2`, or `0,1,2,3` based on the number of mapped people. See the adjacent license/model note before production deployment.

nodes.title: MASKED FACE LOCK — BACKEND + MODEL REQUIREMENTS
widgets_values:
## MASKED FACE IDENTITY LOCK (AFTER THE FHD CROP)

This branch corrects faces on the generated frames, builds a face mask for each frame, and blends only the masked face area back over the untouched generated frame. It does not replace the background, clothes, or the rest of the body.

### Backend values

Set both index strings in **FACE MAP — BACKEND SETS INDEXES** to the active people: 1 person = `0`; 2 = `0,1`; 3 = `0,1,2`; 4 = `0,1,2,3`. The reference is the same backend-composited first frame already loaded in node 1304. Keep people in consistent left-to-right order inside each eight-second chunk; use tracked per-person processing if people cross or heavily occlude each other.

### Required custom nodes and models

Install **ComfyUI-ReActor** and **ComfyUI-Impact-Pack**. Provide `face_yolov8m.pt` under `ComfyUI/models/ultralytics/bbox`, `sam_vit_b_01ec64.pth` under `ComfyUI/models/sams`, and a compatible face-swap model. The included `inswapper_128.onnx` selection is for local testing only. ReActor's documentation says the InsightFace pre-trained `inswapper_128.onnx`/`buffalo_l` models are non-commercial research assets. Replace them with models whose license permits EMB25IA production before deploying.

The frame-list adapters are intentional: they prevent the current Mask Helper batch dimension failure by processing one video frame at a time. Keep them connected.

realtime_target.notes: Always select the untouched original motion video. Never feed a prior generated result back into Character Replacement; repeated VAE passes compound darkness and identity distortion. Keep models resident and use one ComfyUI process per GPU for parallel segments.

quality_1080p.sampling: distilled fixed 8-step first pass plus 3-step detail pass, CFG 1
quality_1080p.multi_person: 1–4 people through the backend-composited edited first frame
quality_1080p.input_rule: Always use the untouched original source video; never reuse generated output.
quality_1080p.duration_rule: Eight-second chunks are trimmed and concatenated to the exact source duration.
quality_1080p.audio_rule: Remux the untouched original audio after concatenation.

backend_contract.profile: LTX-2.5 Ripple multi-person combined FHD + masked face lock
backend_contract.mapping_rule: one stable reference-to-tracked-person mapping for the entire source video
backend_contract.preprocessor_output: one composited edited first frame per 8-second source chunk
backend_contract.gpu_dispatch: one independent ComfyUI worker per GPU; distribute chunks across workers
backend_contract.color_rule: never recursively process generated video; tag final H.264 output as BT.709

post_render_face_lock.mask_scope: face region only; preserve generated background, clothing, and body
post_render_face_lock.batch_safety: convert both image batches to lists before ReActorMaskHelper and rebuild afterward
post_render_face_lock.license_warning: inswapper_128.onnx is selected only as a local-test default; ReActor documents the pre-trained InsightFace inswapper_128/buffalo_l assets as non-commercial research models
